subject: se
question: Differentiate between <<include>> and <<extend>> relationships in a Use Case Diagram, with example and notation.
title: Always Or Sometimes
hook: Making tea ALWAYS includes boiling water. Adding sugar is optional. That is include versus extend.
answer: <<include>>: the base use case ALWAYS uses the included use case; it is mandatory and usually a shared step reused by many use cases.
Notation: dashed arrow labelled <<include>> drawn from the base use case to the included use case. Example: Issue Book <<include>> Check Availability.
<<extend>>: the extending use case adds extra behaviour to the base only under a condition; the base is complete without it (optional).
Notation: dashed arrow labelled <<extend>> drawn from the extending use case to the base use case. Example: Pay Fine <<extend>> Return Book (only if overdue).
Memory trick: include is always, extend is sometimes.
